narrative.overview: The portfolio treats software work as evidence under inspection: finished products remain legible on the surface while precise rules, routes, and system diagrams reveal the engineering underneath. The mood is editorial, technical, calm, and exacting rather than promotional. Warm paper and disciplined graphite establish a tactile publication-like ground. Cobalt appears only as a signal for routes, focus, state, and evidence. Asymmetric compositions and generous pauses prevent the page from feeling like a repeated card catalogue.
keyCharacteristics: Twelve-column editorial alignment with deliberate asymmetry
Inspection geometry built from rules, nodes, routes, and one optical lens
Flat mineral surfaces with restrained optical depth
Purposeful motion that preserves a complete static reading

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Cobalt is the only accent and should occupy a small fraction of any viewport; its rarity gives state changes meaning.

rules.name: The Continuous Paper Rule
rules.body: Sections share one mineral ground. Use rules and spacing—not alternating colored bands—to establish chapters.

rules.name: The Wide Editorial Rule
rules.body: Major statements should form two to four intentional lines, not narrow six-line towers.

rules.name: The Annotation Rule
rules.body: Mono belongs to evidence, sequence, state, and metadata. Narrative prose remains sans-serif.

rules.name: The Shared Datum Rule
rules.body: A rule, image edge, or text block should align to a documented column before it is allowed to break the grid.

rules.name: The One Lens Rule
rules.body: Optical glass is a signature inspection device, not a reusable card treatment.

rules.name: The Flat Evidence Rule
rules.body: Screenshots and diagrams are framed with borders and captions, never generic ambient card shadows.

dos: Do lead project chapters with authentic artifacts or semantic system diagrams.
Do use generous negative space and asymmetric column spans to establish hierarchy.
Do reserve cobalt for interaction, routing, selection, and small proof marks.
Do use CSS for hover/focus, Motion for state transitions, and GSAP only for the signature inspection sequence.
Do preserve complete static content and honor reduced-motion preferences.
Do redesign mobile reading order when desktop composition would become awkward.
donts: Don't return to repeated atlas labels, orange nodes, identical project cards, or bento grids.
Don't use generic SaaS gradients, glowing blobs, widespread glassmorphism, or text gradients.
Don't add decorative particles, stock engineering imagery, fake dashboards, fabricated metrics, or deceptive links.
Don't place the SeeMyUI screenshot in the hero; it is the primary artifact in the selected-work chapter.
Don't animate ordinary hover feedback with GSAP or hide information behind animation.
